<reason>Both sides argued at a high level with clean framing. PRO's opening was the more memorable moral frame ("harassment is a selection mechanism"; "refuse the bundle" separating banter from abuse), and PRO's reversal of CON's throwaway-account example into "a portrait of under-enforcement" was excellent. PRO also answered CON's sharpest turn (identity verification taxing vulnerable players) honestly and effectively by confining friction to post-strike offenders. But CON built the more durable comparative case and handled the endgame better. CON's central distinction — aggression is a different knob from precision, and studios turn the cheap automated one — forced PRO into conceding at [B4.1] that the dumb filter should be turned up with appeals as the cure, which CON then exploited convincingly ("the wrongly flagged player doesn't wait weeks; he uninstalls too, and he's disproportionately the accented or brigaded player"). CON also answered both of PRO's pressure questions squarely: the consent distinction (a per-player setting is not enforcement over objection) neutralized PRO's "your architecture is my motion" capture, and CON named a real consequence for the abuser (loss of audience via reputation-weighted matchmaking that also bites throwaway accounts). PRO's closing then misdescribed that answer as "his target flips a setting," and repeated the correctable-vs-permanent weighing without engaging CON's already-delivered reply. That left CON with the last clean word on the decisive weighing. CON's edge is trimmed by two turns clipped for exceeding the word cap, which cost it the ends of its opening and second rebuttal, so the win is thin rather than comfortable.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's answer to PRO's Q1 plus the follow-up on appeals: by distinguishing a player-controlled default from enforcement imposed over objection, CON blocked PRO's attempted capture of its architecture as "already the motion," and then converted PRO's honest "yes, turn up the filter with appeals" concession into the core indictment — appeals are a slow, same-company queue, so the wrongly flagged accented or brigaded player uninstalls too, collapsing PRO's "correctable error vs permanent loss" weighing.</best_rebuttal>
